segments.text: Arriba Abajo Alcentro Aventro Wendy, here's to your big, beautiful life and your
75th birthday. Wow, Amiga, you made it. 75 amazing rotations around the sun with
incredible style, heart, dedication and compassion. The list of descriptors for
your life work and contributions goes on and on, like a big, beautiful river with
stunning tributaries. You've given so much to the world, personally and
professionally. Gracias, Amiga. Actually, as I reflect on the early days, I'm not
sure I would have dove so deeply into it, etc., as a volunteer river guide and
ultimately as the director, if it were not for you and your Marin VIPs.
Guiding your students on the Stanislaus was my first trip as a checked out ETC guide.
I was so fricking nervous. Going down Bailey Falls, Death Rock and Widowmaker, the
names alone were enough to create white knuckles on the oars. But really, those
early trips on the stand changed my life. And so much of it was the way you
were with your students, your dedication, your belief in their
abilities and the skills that you taught them so that they could live
independent and fully engaged lives were admirable and inspirational.
Flashback, the good night fairies exploring Coral Cave on the Stan, Dutch
oven desserts, forming a human choo-choo train down Rose Creek. And of
course, that insane run down Rainy Falls on the Rogue. Oh, and playing
dulcimers together and singing round a campfire. Then you met Howard and the
gestalt of your lives together was magical and still is. Of course, the boys
drew and read and now their wives, Sarah and Laura, have added so much love
and tender beauty to the family. I'm blessed to call you all, dear, dear
friends, and to have shared so many amazing adventures with you. Rafting
the Rogue and the Middle Fork Salmon, kayaking a spirit to Santo and
well-watching in San Ignacio Lagoon. The list goes on and on. Of course, all
lives come with obstacles. Seeing you navigate the challenges of cancer
like a beautiful warris is admirable. I know it sucks, but your
clarity and steadiness is something to behold. It's like scouting a huge
rapid and then sending off the first guide so we can all watch a
perfect run and learn from it before we take that run. You're always the
teacher and a bad ass river guide. And in this chapter, you are
teaching us all about navigating life. So, Amiga, I want to close this
little birthday missive by saying gracias from the core of my heart.
Thank you for all you continue to give to your family, friends and
community with your wisdom and grace. Arriba, Abajo, Al Centro,
Adentro. Love, Diane. P.S. I know that Brad is on that cosmic
river strumming his beautiful guitar and singing Happy Birthday to
you. Happy Birthday to you. Happy Birthday, dear Wendy. Happy
birthday to you.
